content_of_post_to_comment: I think the worst advice you could give a young scientist is, “Shut up and calculate.” Why should science nurture a myopic insularity? Science has been woven irrevocably into our natural, cultural fabric. A scientist must read poetry, law, philosophy, history, literary criticism, etc. True scientists aspire to participate in the endless, interpretive discussions.
comment: The challenge may be not just encouraging scientists to read broadly, but creating institutions that reward translation between disciplines. Curiosity alone rarely overcomes academic incentives built around specialization.
